examples.text: Bueno, perdonad este momento de locura entre representantes.
examples.trans: Well, forgive this moment of madness between agents.

meanings.note: Identity, profession or a characteristic; compare estar for a state or location.
Also links tratar de + infinitive and forms more than with más de; these uses do not express possession.

examples.text: Llevo más de dos años aquí.
examples.trans: I've been here for more than two years.

examples.text: Te llamo la semana que viene.

meanings.note: Possession, relationships and many fixed expressions.
Tener algo claro means to understand it or have a firm view of it.

examples.text: Tiene muy claro lo que quiere.
examples.trans: She is very clear about what she wants.
Do you have an agent right now?

examples.text: Mi repre me consiguió el papel.
examples.trans: My agent got me the role.

meanings.note: In estar bien or estar mal, evaluates an action or situation.

examples.text: Nada, muy contenta porque estoy grabando una serie

examples.trans: I'll send it to him now.

examples.text: Ya sabes que soy muy clásica.

meanings.note: With a gerund, presents an action developing over time.

examples.text: Poco a poco hemos ido mejorando.

meanings.note: Marks many specific human direct objects without a separate English word; in poco a poco it belongs to the expression little by little.

examples.trans: If I hurry, I'll make it.

examples.text: Guarda la tarjeta en el bolso.
examples.trans: Keep the card in your bag.

Hey, do you have five minutes?

meanings.note: Unstressed direct object; can refer to a statement or idea rather than a masculine physical object.
Links a clause after a judgment in the first lesson example; introduces a relative clause about people in the second.

examples.trans: I'm looking for people who work here.

examples.text: Solamente necesita querer. Y querer es poder, eso está claro, Paquita.
examples.trans: You only need to want it. And where there's a will there's a way, that's clear, Paquita.

examples.text: Todos me han dicho que tú estás muy pasada de moda, que necesito un cambio.
examples.trans: Everyone has told me you're really out of date, and that I need a change.

examples.text: Es que tengo una actriz que necesito que veas. Se llama Lidia San José.
examples.trans: I have an actress I need you to see. Her name is Lidia San José.

meanings.note: A standalone answer can precede a separate negative statement, producing two occurrences of no.
Auxiliary before a past participle; does not express possession.
The impersonal present is hay, not ha.

examples.text: Que si "House of Cards"... No sabía que eso lo veía nadie aquí.
